# Fabrication notes: sentinel-01-4l

Generated by aethelgard 0.1.0 from the specification whose sha256 is
`SPEC_SHA`.
`MANIFEST.json` names every other file of this package by sha256, and the
verdict of the `aethelgard verify` run that emitted the package names every
file, `MANIFEST.json` included. `aethelgard verify --spec <file> --scenarios
<the files MANIFEST.json names> --against-fab <this directory>`, with the
other arguments of the run that emitted it, derives the package again and
names every file that differs. `MANIFEST.json` also names that run's verdict
by sha256, and the verdict states the sandbox each tool ran in, so a run
under another uid or user namespace finds `MANIFEST.json` different while
every other file is the same.

## What this package is

It was emitted by a passing `aethelgard verify`: every gate that verdict
names passed on the design generated from the specification, and these
files were made from that design. The gates judged the design, not these
files. It claims nothing beyond that verdict. Emitting this package made
no board, and nothing in it was tested on hardware.

The Gerbers are KiCad 10.0.7's output (`kicad-cli pcb export gerbers
--check-zones`), exported from a copy of the generated board with the
sha256 the design-rule gate judged, prepared as that gate prepares its copy
(the specification's rules), with every zone refilled by KiCad. KiCad writes the time of export into two lines of every Gerber
(`%TF.CreationDate` and `G04 Created by KiCad ... date`). Those two lines
are removed so that the package is reproducible; nothing else in any file
is changed. The drill file (`kicad-cli pcb export drill
--excellon-min-header`) and the placement file (`kicad-cli pcb export pos
--format csv --units mm --side both`) are KiCad's output, unchanged. KiCad's
Gerber job file is not included; this file states the stackup.

## Stackup

- 4 copper layers, top to bottom, joined only by through vias:
  - F.Cu: signal
  - In1.Cu: plane, net GND
  - In2.Cu: plane, net VDD_3V3
  - B.Cu: signal
- Each dielectric at least:
  - F.Cu to In1.Cu: 0.179 mm (OSH Park 4-layer, docs.oshpark.com/services/four-layer/, read 14 Nov 2026: 2113 prepreg 0.1999 mm less 0.0202 mm, rounded down)
  - In1.Cu to In2.Cu: 0.891 mm (OSH Park 4-layer, docs.oshpark.com/services/four-layer/, read 14 Nov 2026: FR408HR core 0.9906 mm less 0.0991 mm, rounded down)
  - In2.Cu to B.Cu: 0.179 mm (OSH Park 4-layer, docs.oshpark.com/services/four-layer/, read 14 Nov 2026: 2113 prepreg 0.1999 mm less 0.0202 mm, rounded down)
- Thickness source: OSH Park 4-layer, docs.oshpark.com/services/four-layer/, read 14 Nov 2026: min the dielectric minima summed; max dielectrics and resist at max plus 4 x 70 um copper, 1.8505 mm up. Copper source: the engine's stated condition (AET-WO-1305, as the reference): 2 oz, twice KiCad's 35 um; OSH Park publishes no copper tolerance.
- Every minimum here is its source's value less its published tolerance, rounded down; every maximum, rounded up.
- Laminate: as the dielectrics' sources above state, with laminate and solder mask relative permittivity at
  most 5.4 (the IPC-4101 FR-4 maximum, specified at 1 MHz).
- Declared thickness 1.6 mm. Finished board from 1.25 mm to 1.851 mm thick.
- Finished copper at most 70 um thick on each layer.

A board made outside this stackup is not covered by the capacitance bound
of `aethelgard extract`. That bound's scope and conditions, as `extract`
states them:

- scope: the bare board's copper and each I2C pin's Ci; part bodies, solder and terminations above the pads are not included
- laminate and solder mask relative permittivity at most 5.4 (the IPC-4101 FR-4 maximum, specified at 1 MHz)
- finished copper at most 70 um thick; finished board from 1.25 mm to 1.851 mm thick
- each dielectric at least its declared minimum: F.Cu to In1.Cu 0.179 mm, In1.Cu to In2.Cu 0.891 mm, In2.Cu to B.Cu 0.179 mm
- zone fill keeps the board's clearance (the DRC gate refills and judges it)
- every I2C pin at most UM10204's Ci of 10 pF; no multiplexer or switch on the line
- neighbouring nets are static while the line rises


## Holes

Every hole is a plated via, drilled 0.3 mm, with a 0.6 mm pad. The
drill file is Excellon, metric, with decimal coordinates, and its minimal
header carries no plating comment.

## Rule minima

- Track width: 0.2 mm.
- Copper to copper: 0.2 mm.
- Via: 0.6 mm pad, 0.3 mm drill.

## Acknowledged ledger rows

The witness ledger classes these register fields as judged by no independent rule, model or bench reading. The specification acknowledges each by name, with its reason, and the bench reads them (`RUL-20`):

- `FLASH.OPTSR_CUR` (silicon-only): `BOR_LEV`. Level 0, the factory value (RM0433 Rev 9 Table 21, p. 177), so FAB-NOTES carries no step; no model, the twin presents it (4230 FEEDBACK section 2 m1). The bench row reads bits 3:2 as 00.
- `GPIOA.AFRL` (same-source): `AFSEL5`, `AFSEL6`, `AFSEL7`. PA5-PA7 at AF5 for SPI1: the model routes a pin by AFR only for a timer channel (4300 FEEDBACK section 0). The bench row reads AFRL back.
- `GPIOA.MODER` (same-source): `MODER0`, `MODER5`, `MODER6`, `MODER7`. PA0 output (flash CS) and PA5-PA7 alternate for SPI1: a BSRR write drives a pin whatever MODER says (4200 FEEDBACK). The bench row reads MODER back.
- `GPIOA.OSPEEDR` (same-source): `OSPEED0`, `OSPEED5`, `OSPEED6`, `OSPEED7`. PA0 and SPI1's PA5-PA7: no edge rate is modelled; check speeds judges each chosen speed's fmax with svd-hal's own table, not an ir rule. The bench row reads OSPEEDR back.
- `GPIOA.OTYPER` (ignored-by-model): `OT0`, `OT1`, `OT2`, `OT3`, `OT4`, `OT5`, `OT6`, `OT7`, `OT8`, `OT9`, `OT10`, `OT11`, `OT12`, `OT13`, `OT14`, `OT15`. OTYPER is not stored by Renode (4300b FEEDBACK section 10, measured): written whole, push-pull on every port A pin. The bench row reads it back.
- `GPIOA.PUPDR` (same-source): `PUPD0`, `PUPD1`, `PUPD2`, `PUPD3`, `PUPD4`, `PUPD5`, `PUPD6`, `PUPD7`, `PUPD8`, `PUPD9`, `PUPD10`, `PUPD11`, `PUPD12`, `PUPD13`, `PUPD14`, `PUPD15`. No pull is modelled. Written whole by split: no pull on the solved pins, the debug pins' reset pulls (PA13 up, PA14 down, PA15 up) kept. The bench row reads PUPDR back.
- `GPIOB.AFRL` (same-source): `AFSEL6`, `AFSEL7`. PB6/PB7 at AF4 for I2C1: the model routes a pin by AFR only for a timer channel (4300 FEEDBACK section 0). The bench row reads AFRL back.
- `GPIOB.MODER` (same-source): `MODER6`, `MODER7`. PB6/PB7 alternate for I2C1: the model routes a pin by MODER only for a timer channel (4300 FEEDBACK section 0). The bench row reads MODER back.
- `GPIOB.OSPEEDR` (same-source): `OSPEED6`, `OSPEED7`. PB6/PB7 for I2C1 at 400 kHz: no edge rate is modelled; check speeds judges the chosen speed's fmax with svd-hal's own table, not an ir rule. The bench row reads OSPEEDR back.
- `GPIOB.OTYPER` (ignored-by-model): `OT0`, `OT1`, `OT2`, `OT3`, `OT4`, `OT5`, `OT6`, `OT7`, `OT8`, `OT9`, `OT10`, `OT11`, `OT12`, `OT13`, `OT14`, `OT15`. OTYPER is not stored by Renode (4300b FEEDBACK section 10): PB6/PB7 open-drain for I2C1, the rest push-pull. The bench row reads it back.
- `GPIOB.PUPDR` (same-source): `PUPD0`, `PUPD1`, `PUPD2`, `PUPD3`, `PUPD4`, `PUPD5`, `PUPD6`, `PUPD7`, `PUPD8`, `PUPD9`, `PUPD10`, `PUPD11`, `PUPD12`, `PUPD13`, `PUPD14`, `PUPD15`. No pull is modelled. Written whole by split: no internal pull on PB6/PB7 (the bus has 2.2 kOhm), PB4's reset pull-up kept. The bench row reads PUPDR back.
- `I2C1.CR1` (same-source): `PE`. PE is set by the enable, not by silicon::i2c_cr1 (whose word has PE clear); stored, with no reaction claimed. The bench row reads PE as 1.
- `I2C1.CR2` (same-source): `ADD10`, `HEAD10R`, `STOP`, `NACK`, `RELOAD`, `AUTOEND`, `PECBYTE`. 7-bit addressing, no reload, no PEC, written 0 (AUTOEND set at run time): STM32F7_I2C.cs is not held, no reaction claimed. The bench row reads CR2 back, all but AUTOEND.
- `I2C1.ICR` (same-source): `ADDRCF`, `NACKCF`, `STOPCF`, `BERRCF`, `ARLOCF`, `OVRCF`, `PECCF`, `TIMOUTCF`, `ALERTCF`. Write-1-to-clear (RM0433 Rev 9 section 47.9.8, p. 2015), so no bench row: STOPCF and NACKCF after each transfer. The next record's OK status on silicon shows the clear took.
- `RCC.CR` (ignored-by-model): `D2CKRDY`. Not polled (ruling on Q-F): STM32H7_RCC.cs L175 keeps it a tag reading 0, so a wait would park every boot. Silicon must read 1 after a D2 enable: a bench row.
- `RCC.D1CCIPR` (ignored-by-model): `CKPERSEL`. A tag in Renode (STM32H7_RCC.cs L401, read 0 whatever is written, 4230 FEEDBACK section 2). SPI1's kernel per_ck assumes HSI here; the bench row reads it.
- `RCC.D2CCIP1R` (ignored-by-model): `SPI123SEL`, `SPI45SEL`. ResetClock reads them at reset before the select write; a tag (STM32H7_RCC.cs L408-410) reads 0 whatever silicon holds. The written SPI123SEL is judged by spi_words.
- `RCC.D2CCIP2R` (ignored-by-model): `USART16SEL`, `USART28SEL`, `I2C123SEL`. Left at reset: I2C123SEL's rcc_pclk1 is what check_timingr assumes; ResetClock reads the USART selects though no port uses them. A tag in Renode (L420-425); the bench row reads each.
- `SCB.CPACR` (same-source): `CP10`, `CP11`. The FPU enable in the generated Reset, outside every Kani harness; whether Renode faults a float with CPACR clear is not held. The bench row reads CP10/CP11 as full access.
- `SPI1.CR2` (ignored-by-model): `TSER`. A tag (STM32H7_SPI.cs L149), written 0 with TSIZE: no reload is used. The bench row reads it back as 0.
- `SPI1.IFCR` (ignored-by-model): `TXTFC`, `UDRC`, `OVRC`, `CRCEC`, `TIFREC`, `MODFC`, `TSERFC`. Tags in Renode (STM32H7_SPI.cs L258-266), written 0 beside EOTC; write-only, so no bench row. The boot record's flash identity, read on silicon, shows each transfer ended.
- `SPI1.SR` (ignored-by-model): `MODF`. MODF is a tag (STM32H7_SPI.cs L238) and MASTER always reads 1: no mode fault in the twin. SSM|SSI before SPE is proved by Kani; the bench row reads MODF as 0.
